type.title: Type

protocol.title: Protocol
protocol.description: Protocol is the inference API protocol served by the Service.

operation.title: Operation
operation.description: Operation is the inference operation of a request, normalized across the protocols. It names what a request does rather than which route it arrived on, so a rule that matches the generation traffic of a Cluster is one term rather than a disjunction over every protocol that spells generation differently, and a rule written for one protocol keeps working for a Service that later serves another. The Protocol enum alongside it, and the request path, identify the exact route wherever that matters.

route.title: Route
route.description: Route is the canonical inference API route of the request. It names the exact surface that the request arrived on, which the Operation field deliberately does not, so it is what a rule that has to distinguish two routes of the same protocol reads.

source.title: Source
source.description: Source is what produced the response

isUpstreamInvoked.description: IsUpstreamInvoked is set for the requests whose inference upstream actually responded. It is not the same fact as the Source field: a response that a Guardrail Plugin blocked has a Source of OCTELIUM and was still generated by the upstream, and therefore still cost whatever the Usage field reports. It is what separates the requests that were rejected before the upstream ran from the ones that were rejected after it did.

model.description: Model shows which model the request named and which one served it

stream.description: Stream is set for the requests that asked for a streamed response

maxOutputTokens.description: MaxOutputTokens is the maximum output token count that the downstream itself requested. It is zero whenever the request declares none.

inputItemCount.description: InputItemCount is the number of the input items (i.e. the messages or the embedding inputs) of the request

hasImageInput.description: HasImageInput is set for the requests that carry image input

hasAudioInput.description: HasAudioInput is set for the requests that carry audio input

estimatedInputTokens.description: EstimatedInputTokens is Octelium's own pre-flight input token estimate. It is always set for the parsed inference requests regardless of the Usage field, and it must never be treated as a billing truth. Read the EstimateQuality field alongside it.

estimateQuality.title: Estimate Quality
estimateQuality.description: EstimateQuality is whether the EstimatedInputTokens field accounted for the entire input of the request

usage.description: Usage is the token usage reported by the upstream provider itself

responseID.description: ResponseID is the response identifier reported by the upstream provider itself

finishReason.title: Finish Reason
finishReason.description: FinishReason is the completion status of the response, normalized across the providers. The providers spell the same outcome differently (e.g. `stop`, `end_turn` and `STOP` all mean that the model finished on its own), so a chart that grouped on the raw value would split one outcome into one slice per protocol.

rawFinishReason.description: RawFinishReason is the completion status exactly as the upstream provider spelled it (e.g. "stop", "end_turn", "max_tokens"). It is kept alongside the normalized FinishReason field for the investigations that need the provider's own vocabulary.

timeToFirstToken.description: TimeToFirstToken is the duration between accepting the request and the first generated content of a streamed response

eventCount.description: EventCount is the number of the events of a streamed response, whether they are the events of a `text/event-stream` or the messages of the AWS event stream that the BEDROCK protocol serves

reasoning.description: Reasoning is the reasoning configuration that the upstream was served

tools.description: Tools is the tool surface that the request carried

guardrails.description: Guardrails is the outcome of every Guardrail Plugin that was applied to the request, one entry per Plugin and leg

tokenRateLimit.description: TokenRateLimit is the outcome of the token quota enforcement

semanticCache.description: SemanticCache is the outcome of the SemanticCache Plugin

semanticRouter.description: SemanticRouter is the outcome of the SemanticRouter Plugin

translation.description: Translation is the record of a request whose upstream protocol differed from the one that the downstream used. It is unset for the requests that were not translated at all.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: LLM is the LLM-gateway-specific information

result.title: Result
result.description: Result is the outcome that the Plugin reached on the leg

leg.title: Leg
leg.description: Leg is the part of the exchange that is inspected

plugin.description: Plugin is the name of the Guardrail Plugin

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.title:
Note that the Usage, ResponseID, RawFinishReason and Model.Reported
 fields of a translated entry are the ones that the upstream itself
 reported rather than the ones that the translated response carried,
 since a translation regenerates the response identifier and spells
 the completion status in the downstream's own vocabulary. The Usage
 counts therefore follow the accounting of the UpstreamProtocol
 rather than of the entry's own `protocol` field, which matters for
 the cache token counts that the two protocols account for
 differently.
octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: Note that the Usage, ResponseID, RawFinishReason and Model.Reported fields of a translated entry are the ones that the upstream itself reported rather than the ones that the translated response carried, since a translation regenerates the response identifier and spells the completion status in the downstream's own vocabulary. The Usage counts therefore follow the accounting of the UpstreamProtocol rather than of the entry's own `protocol` field, which matters for the cache token counts that the two protocols account for differently.  Guardrail is the outcome that one Guardrail Plugin reached on one leg of the exchange. A request carries one of them per applied Plugin and leg rather than a single summary, since a redaction that one Plugin performed is a security event in its own right and it would be lost by a record that only kept the strongest outcome of the request.

requested.description: Requested is the model name requested by the downstream, verbatim. It is set even for the requests that Octelium rejected, since it is read from the request itself.

effective.description: Effective is the model name that Octelium proxied to the upstream. It differs from the Requested one exactly when the Source field is set, which is the record of the Service overriding what the downstream asked for.

reported.description: Reported is the model name that the upstream provider itself named in its response. It resolves the aliases and the unpinned names that the Effective one can carry, and for a request that the SemanticCache served it is the model that generated the cached response rather than one that was invoked now.

source.title: Source
source.description: Source is what decided the Effective model

plugin.description: Plugin is the name of the Plugin that decided the Effective model. It is empty whenever the Source is not a Plugin.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.title: Model
octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: Model shows which model the request named and which one served it

isDisabled.description: IsDisabled is set for the requests that were proxied with reasoning explicitly turned off

effort.description: Effort is the ordinal reasoning effort that was served to the upstream, verbatim. It is empty for the models that accept a numeric budget instead.

tokenBudget.description: TokenBudget is the reasoning token budget that was served to the upstream. It is zero for the models that accept an ordinal effort instead.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.title: Reasoning
octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: Reasoning is the reasoning configuration that the upstream was actually served. It is only set for the requests whose reasoning configuration the Service itself decided, since Octelium does not read the one that a downstream sets for itself.

result.title: Result
result.description: Result is the outcome of the cache lookup

similarity.description: Similarity is the cosine similarity of the entry that was served. It is only set for a SEMANTIC_HIT.

isStored.description: IsStored is set for the requests whose response was stored in the cache

plugin.description: Plugin is the name of the SemanticCache Plugin that was applied

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.title: Semantic Cache
octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: SemanticCache is the outcome of the SemanticCache Plugin

result.title: Result
result.description: Result is the outcome of the routing decision

route.description: Route is the name of the Route of the Plugin that matched. It is only set for a MATCH. Note that it is unrelated to the LLM entry's own `route` field, which names the inference API surface instead.

similarity.description: Similarity is the cosine similarity at which the Route matched. It is only set for a MATCH.

model.description: Model is the model that the Plugin selected. Note that it is not necessarily the model that the request was eventually served with, since a Model Plugin overwrites it.

plugin.description: Plugin is the name of the SemanticRouter Plugin that reached the decision

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.title: Semantic Router
octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: SemanticRouter is the outcome of the SemanticRouter Plugin. It is recorded separately from the Model field because a Model Plugin overwrites the model that the SemanticRouter selected, which would otherwise erase every trace that the request was routed at all.

result.title: Result
result.description: Result is the outcome of the quota enforcement

plugin.description: Plugin is the name of the TokenRateLimit Plugin that denied the request. It is empty for an ALLOWED result, since no single Plugin decided it.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Scope sets which of the token counts of a request are counted against the limit

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.title: Token Rate Limit
octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: TokenRateLimit is the outcome of the token quota enforcement of the request. It is a single record rather than one per Plugin because the enforcement has a single outcome: every applied Plugin has to admit the request, so a denial is always the decision of exactly one of them and an admission is the decision of none of them in particular. The per-Plugin reservation and charge counts are deliberately not recorded, since they are quantities of separate quotas that cannot be summed into one number.

count.description: Count is the number of the tools that the upstream was offered, after every Tools Plugin was applied

names.description: Names is the sorted list of the names of those tools. It is bounded, so a request that declares an unusually large number of them carries a sample rather than a complete list, which is visible as a Names list shorter than the Count field.

removedCount.description: RemovedCount is the number of the tools that the downstream declared and that a Tools Plugin removed before the request was proxied

removedNames.description: RemovedNames is the sorted list of the names of those removed tools. It is the record of what the downstream tried to expose to the model and was not allowed to, which is the question that the RemovedCount field alone cannot answer. It is bounded in the same way as the Names field.

calledNames.description: CalledNames is the sorted list of the distinct names of the tools that the model asked to invoke in its response. It is the record of what the model tried to do rather than of what it was allowed to do, which is why it is kept separately from the Names field. Note that it is a set of identities rather than a count of calls: read the CallCount field for the latter.

callCount.description: CallCount is the number of the tool calls that the response carried. It counts the calls rather than the distinct tools, so a response that invoked one tool twenty times has a CallCount of twenty and a single CalledNames entry.

isCalledNamesTruncated.description: IsCalledNamesTruncated is set whenever the response carried more distinct tool identities than the CalledNames list can hold. It exists because the absence of a name from a bounded list is not evidence that the tool was not called, and a security dashboard that treated it as such would report a false negative.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.title: Tools
octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: Tools is the tool surface that the request carried

upstreamProtocol.title: Protocol
upstreamProtocol.description: Protocol is the inference API protocol served by the Service.

upstreamRoute.title: Route
upstreamRoute.description: Route is the canonical inference API route of the request. It names the exact surface that the request arrived on, which the Operation field deliberately does not, so it is what a rule that has to distinguish two routes of the same protocol reads.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.title: Translation
octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: Translation is the record of a request whose upstream protocol differed from the one that the downstream used. It is only set for the requests that Octelium actually translated, so its absence means that the upstream spoke the entry's own `protocol` field. The downstream protocol and route are deliberately not repeated here, since the entry already carries them.

state.title: State
state.description: State is whether the reported usage is the final one

inputTokens.description: InputTokens is the number of the input/prompt tokens

outputTokens.description: OutputTokens is the number of the generated/completion tokens

totalTokens.description: TotalTokens is the total token count reported by the upstream provider itself. Whenever the provider reports none, which is the case for the ANTHROPIC protocol as well as for many OpenAI-compatible servers, it is computed as the sum of the input and output tokens plus only those cache token counts that the provider accounts for additively (i.e. the ANTHROPIC ones). The OPENAI cached and reasoning token counts are already included in the input and the output counts respectively and they are therefore never added again.

cacheReadInputTokens.description: CacheReadInputTokens is the number of the input tokens that were read from the provider's prompt cache. Note that the providers account for it differently: it is a subset of the InputTokens field for the OPENAI protocol while it is additive to it for the ANTHROPIC one.

cacheWriteInputTokens.description: CacheWriteInputTokens is the number of the input tokens that were written to the provider's prompt cache. It is only reported by the ANTHROPIC protocol and it is additive to the InputTokens field.

reasoningOutputTokens.description: ReasoningOutputTokens is the number of the reasoning tokens. It is only reported by the OPENAI protocol where it is already included in the OutputTokens field.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.title: Usage
octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: Usage is the token usage of the request as reported by the upstream provider itself. It is only set for the requests whose provider reported one at all, so it never carries an Octelium estimate and it is unset for a request that the SemanticCache served, which invoked no inference at all. Summing its counts is therefore a sum of the tokens that were really consumed rather than of a mixture of measurements and guesses. Read the EstimatedInputTokens field for the requests that carry no usage.

isProtocolError.description: IsProtocolError is set when the response carried a JSON-RPC `error`

errorCode.description: ErrorCode is the JSON-RPC error code of the response (e.g. -32601 for `Method not found` or -32020 for `HeaderMismatch`)

errorMessage.description: ErrorMessage is the JSON-RPC error message of the response

isToolError.description: IsToolError is set when the method is `tools/call` and the successful result carried an `isError` value. This is a different layer from the ErrorCode field: the call succeeded at the protocol layer while the tool itself failed.

eventCount.description: EventCount is the number of the `text/event-stream` events of the response

notificationCount.description: NotificationCount is the number of the JSON-RPC notifications, such as progress notifications, of the response stream

ttlMs.description: TTLMs is the `ttlMs` cache freshness hint of the result, if set

cacheScope.description: CacheScope is the `cacheScope` of the result, if set (e.g. "public")

client.description: Client is the client information reported by the downstream itself. It is NOT an identity.

sessionID.description: SessionID is the value of the `Mcp-Session-Id` header used by the protocol revisions between 2025-03-26 and 2025-11-25. It is an MCP transport identifier that is unrelated to the Octelium Session as well as to the AccessLog entry's own sessionID field.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: SessionRequestExec is the details of a session exec request

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: SessionRequestSubsystem is the details of a session subsystem request

requestedUser.description: RequestedUser is the requested SSH user by the downstream.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.title: Start
octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: Start is the details of a new SSH connection

type.title: Type
type.description: Type is the TCP-specific type of the entry

receivedBytes.description: ReceivedBytes is the number of bytes received from downstream. Only used with END entries.

sentBytes.description: SentBytes is the number of bytes sent to downstream. Only used with END entries.

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: TCP is the TCP-specific information

octelium.api.main.core.v1.AccessLog.Entr.description: UDP is the UDP-specific information

milliseconds.description: Milliseconds is the duration set in milliseconds

seconds.description: Seconds is the duration set in seconds

minutes.description: Minutes is the duration set in minutes

hours.description: Hours is the duration set in hours

days.description: Days is the duration set in days

weeks.description: Weeks is the duration set in weeks

months.description: Months is the duration set in months

octelium.api.main.meta.v1.Duration.title: Duration
octelium.api.main.meta.v1.Duration.description: Duration is a length of time that is expressed in a single unit of choice. Exactly one of the units is set (e.g. `seconds: 30`).

id.description: ID is the unique ID for the log entry

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is the timestamp of creation.

actorRef.description: ActorRef is the reference of the actor whose action triggered the log entry (i.e. the User, their Session and Device if available)

targetRef.description: TargetRef is the reference of the target of the action that triggered the log entry (e.g. the Service and its Namespace in the case of a SERVICE log entry)

octelium.api.main.meta.v1.LogMetadata.title: Log Metadata
octelium.api.main.meta.v1.LogMetadata.description: LogMetadata is the metadata that is common to every log entry (i.e. the AccessLogs and the ComponentLogs). It is the log-entry counterpart of the Metadata of the Cluster resources.

apiVersion.description: APIVersion is the API version of the reference resource

kind.description: Kind is the resource kind. A kind is unique per an APIVersion.

uid.description: UID is the resource object UID. A UID is unique across the entire Cluster.

name.description: Name is the resource object name. A name is unique per a certain kind.

resourceVersion.description: ResourceVersion is the resourceVersion of the resource.

octelium.api.main.meta.v1.ObjectReferenc.title: Object Reference
octelium.api.main.meta.v1.ObjectReferenc.description: ObjectReference is a reference to another Cluster resource. It identifies the referenced resource by its kind and either its UID or its name.
